sarah: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about an async eviction coordinator that cooperates with the existing slab allocator. want to debate interface boundaries, compaction triggers, and safe preemption.

kai: High-level thought: coordinator should nominate victim segments and request reclaim hints from slab. question: do we expose a small API like `reclaim_hint(size_bytes)` or a richer iterator over allocations?

omar: I'd lean `reclaim_hint` (best-effort). exposing iterators leaks allocator internals and couples modules. also avoids long blocking scans.

devon: Agree on best-effort. we should also support incremental compaction windows to avoid long tail latency (e.g., 10ms work slices between inference batches). keep compaction preemptible.

sarah: Metrics we need up front: `reclaimable_bytes`, `avg_reclaim_latency_ms`, `compaction_progress_pct`, and `pinned_conflicts`. plus histograms for free-run lengths.

kai: On pinned tensors: coordinator must respect a `pin` flag and never attempt DMA out for pinned allocations. For pageable GPU objects we can overlap async GPU->host copy + free on completion.

omar: Edge case: severe fragmentation where total free bytes > needed but no contiguous region. Idea: maintain a sparse segment table and allow targeted defrag hints: coordinator can say `defrag(segment_id, min_contig)` so slab coalesces local holes.

devon: Example pseudo flow: ```
// coordinator asks for reclaim
coordinator.request_reclaim(segment_id, bytes_needed);
// slab tries limited coalesce work
slab.on_reclaim_hint(segment_id)->try_coalesce(10ms);
```

infra-bot: CI: fuzz-allocator-sim run started on queue-7 (job #8843).

kai: Testing plan: 1) microbench deterministic fuzz harness with controlled allocation sizes, 2) steady-state throughput run (1000 tokens/s) with occasional big batches, 3) chaos test with pinned flags toggled.

sarah: Action items I will own: 1) draft `reclaim_hint` API (sync best-effort) + doc, 2) prototype incremental compaction worker, 3) run sim with 1M random allocations and capture fragmentation curves.

omar: One more policy note: fallback to host eviction only when `free_ratio < tenant_threshold` (configurable per tenant/priority). avoid host-thrashing for high-priority customers.

devon: Also measure async-copy CPU/GPU overlap cost. if GPU->host copy latency threatens token SLO, we should prefer light-weight quantized model fallback instead of aggressive eviction.

kai: :thumbsup: good plan. can we sync tomorrow 10:00 for 30m?

sarah: @kai yes 10:00 works. I'll open the follow-up PR and link the sim logs in the thread.
